speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Prime Minister what measures are being taken to ensure that (i) the minimisation of the risk that SGX-listed companies experience a sudden deterioration in financial viability and (ii) SGX RegCo is sufficiently resourced to discharge its obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The financial performance of companies depends on many factors, such as the global business conditions, competition, performance of specific projects, and also its own business decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: That is why investing in listed companies entails risks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Investors in search of returns must understand that returns come with risks.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our regulatory regime does not, and cannot, dictate how listed companies make their commercial decisions or seek to prevent business failures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: What regulation can do is to promote transparency and good disclosure practices so that investors are able to make informed decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This includes reporting financial results either quarterly or half-yearly, depending on their market capitalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Further, if the board sees clear evidence of significant improvement or deterioration in the company’s near-term financial performance, it is obliged to make an immediate announcement.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As the frontline regulator, SGX RegCo, monitors listed companies’ compliance with disclosure requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If they are inadequate or lack clarity, SGX RegCo will, either by way of public queries or by directly engaging the listed company, elicit further disclosures.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For serious disclosure lapses or irregularities, SGX RegCo will investigate and take appropriate enforcement actions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As to the question whether SGX RegCo is sufficiently resourced, RegCo did not start from scratch.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: When it was constituted last year, it took over all the existing regulatory functions and resources of SGX.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: A separate board with a majority of independent directors was then formed with the sole responsibility of overseeing SGX RegCo's performance of its regulatory functions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This was aimed at ensuring the independence and dedicated focus of SGX's regulatory functions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX RegCo also remains supervised by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX RegCo, like most reputable regulators, takes a risk-based approach in determining where to focus its efforts and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Its efforts to respond in a timelier manner to potential cases of corporate malfeasance have also been well-received by the market.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX RegCo will continue to build up its capabilities and strive to ensure that listed companies abide by high standards of corporate governance and disclosure practices.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There have been a number of cases in recent years of SGX-listed firms which have seen a sudden deterioration in financial viability, leading to investors losing huge sums of money, including some retail investors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Of course, some of this is unavoidable and it is due to business conditions and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, the key is really about transparency, disclosure, so that investors can know all the risks that they are facing.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this regard, in the past, there have been concerns raised by third parties about the accuracy of accounts or non-disclosure of certain pertinent information, and some of these concerns have been publicised, in a few cases, long before the deterioration occurred.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I just have a few supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There had been cases of non-disclosure of information, negligence in preparation and release of financial statements and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, are SGX RegCo and MAS very committed to imposing penalties for non-disclosure of information that could be price-sensitive, that could affect the share price, when it is revealed that certain information was not disclosed?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because there have been concerns raised by commentators that this was not done at certain times and certain instances in the past.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Lastly, what does SGX do to engage stakeholders, such as experts in corporate governance, Investors Association, and so on, to enable them to understand the approach taken by SGX RegCo towards reports of financial irregularities or governance lapses, to ensure that they understand and make use of existing channels, and also to take feedback and improve the process?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It would appear to be a continuing concern that, in the words of Prof Mak Yuen Teen, a corporate governance expert, on his blog in October last year, "Often, investors who wrote to me have, in fact, told me that they have received either no replies or boilerplate replies from the regulators.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It may be that the regulators are doing something, but it is such a black box, and often such a slow process, that it gives the impression that nothing is being done".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are four questions, but I think they are all related.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The general answer on timeliness, penalties, whether SGX RegCo engages experts, take feedback, is all yes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we have to understand the nature of investigations: you can take feedback but there are all kinds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some, not so credible, you may have to put aside; some more credible, especially if they put their names behind, and you investigate, but you may not want to reply and talk about it publicly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Usually, investigations, by their nature, are quiet until you get enough evidence, before you mount a more robust investigation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And all, of course, this has to be done in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you need expert advice, you ask for them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If any wrongdoers are caught, of course, they have to face the full force of the law.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This has been SGX RegCo's, MAS' and the Commercial Affairs Department's approach as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The Member did mention there were instances where this was not observed, or where there was no follow-up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We need to know what those instances are.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Give us specific examples and we will be happy to look into them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think the Member may have in mind the case of Noble Group.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am guessing here that when the Member said there were instances, he may be thinking of Noble Group.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There were reports written by Iceberg Research about the irregularities in accounting practices.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have always taken the allegations levelled by Iceberg Research seriously.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, like all investigations, you must have some evidence to start with.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, they probed further and, at a certain point, the authorities had enough basis to start overt investigations.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are the circumstances surrounding Noble Group, in particular.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I would say, in general, we take allegations seriously, we investigate them, seek expert advice.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If there are wrongdoers, they have to face the full force of the law.
